subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 11
topic: Fractions, decimals, percentages and ratio (Term 1B) · Calculator · Higher
intro: You may use a calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks are given even when the final answer is wrong, and on questions that say "show your working" an answer with no working gets 0 marks. Give fractions and ratios in their simplest form. Give money answers to 2 decimal places where needed. Read the last line of each question again before you answer, to check what it asks for.

questions.q: Which of these is equal to 2.4?
Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
Write 340 as a percentage. (%)

Work out 416 − 11112
Show your working. Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Type a mixed number with a space, like 2 3/4 (or an improper fraction like 11/4)
questions.ms: Answer: 2 1/4. M1 for 25/6 − 23/12 written as 50/12 − 23/12 (or 3 + 1/6 − 11/12). A1 for 2 1/4 (accept 9/4). 2 3/12 not simplified: M1 A0. Check the final fraction can't be simplified.

questions.q:
Work out 412 ÷ 145
Show your working. Give your answer as a mixed number.
questions.hint: Type a mixed number with a space, like 2 3/4 (or an improper fraction like 11/4)
questions.ms: Answer: 2 1/2. M1 for 9/2 × 5/9 (improper fractions, flip the second, multiply). A1 for 2 1/2 (accept 5/2).

questions.q:
You are told that 23 × 47 = 1081.
Use this fact to write down the value of 2.3 × 0.47
questions.ms: Answer: 1.081. B1. 2.3 × 0.47 has 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places, so 1081 → 1.081.

questions.q: Use 23 × 47 = 1081 to write down the value of 1081 ÷ 4.7
questions.ms: Answer: 230. B1. 1081 ÷ 47 = 23, and 4.7 is 10 times smaller than 47, so the answer is 10 times bigger: 230.

questions.q:
Use algebra to show that the recurring decimal 0.3̇6̇ (which means 0.363636…) is equal to 4/11.
Follow these steps in the working box:
Step 1: Write x = 0.363636…
Step 2: Two digits repeat, so multiply by 100. Write down 100x.
Step 3: Subtract to get rid of the recurring part: 100x − x = …
Step 4: Solve for x and simplify the fraction.
questions.ms: M1 for x = 0.3636… and 100x = 36.3636… M1 for subtracting: 99x = 36. A1 for x = 36/99 = 4/11 (divide top and bottom by 9). Just writing 4 ÷ 11 = 0.3636… on a calculator: 0 marks, because the question asks for algebra.

questions.q:
A school has 840 students. 27 of them walk to school. 58 of the rest come by bus. All the others come by car.
How many students come by car?
questions.ms: Answer: 225. M1 for walkers = 240, so the rest = 600. M1 for bus = 5/8 × 600 = 375. A1 for 600 − 375 = 225. Common mistake: taking 5/8 of 840 instead of 5/8 of the rest.

questions.q: Which number do you multiply by to decrease an amount by 12%?

A car costs AED 80 000. Its value goes down by 10% every year (depreciation).
Work out the value of the car after 3 years. (AED)
questions.ms: Answer: AED 58 320. M1 for using 0.9 (or finding 10% and subtracting for one year: 72 000). M1 for 80 000 × 0.9³ or three correct years (72 000, 64 800). A1 for 58 320. 80 000 − 3 × 8000 = 56 000 (simple): M1 at most.

questions.q:
Sara has AED 6000 to invest for 4 years.
Bank A pays 3% compound interest per year.
Bank B pays 3.2% simple interest per year.
Which bank pays more interest, and by how much? Write the bank in your working and type the difference in AED in the answer box.
questions.ms: Answer: Bank B, by AED 14.95. M1 for 6000 × 1.03⁴ (= 6753.05). M1 for Bank B interest 6000 × 0.032 × 4 = 768 (or total 6768). M1 for comparing like with like: interest 753.05 and 768 (or totals 6753.05 and 6768). A1 for Bank B and 14.95 (accept 14.94 to 14.95).

questions.q:
The price of a phone goes up by 8%. The new price is AED 3240.
What was the price before the increase? (AED)
questions.ms: Answer: AED 3000. M1 for 3240 = 108% of the original. M1 for 3240 ÷ 1.08. A1 for 3000. Common mistake: taking 8% off 3240 (2980.80): 0 marks.

questions.q:
A shop buys a lamp for AED 64 and sells it for AED 88.
Work out the percentage profit. (%)
questions.ms: Answer: 37.5%. M1 for 24 ÷ 64 (profit ÷ cost price) × 100. A1 for 37.5. Dividing by 88 (27.3%): 0 marks.

questions.q: Write 45 minutes : 2 hours as a ratio in its simplest form.
questions.ms: Answer: 3 : 8. B1. Change to the same units first: 45 : 120, then divide by 15.

questions.q: Write the ratio 8 : 20 in the form 1 : n. Type the value of n.
questions.ms: Answer: n = 2.5. B1. Divide both sides by 8: 1 : 2.5.

questions.q:
In a bag, the ratio of red counters to blue counters is 3 : 7.
What fraction of the counters are red?
questions.ms: B1: 3/10. There are 3 + 7 = 10 parts altogether, and 3 of them are red.

questions.q:
Huda and Sami share some money in the ratio 7 : 4. Huda gets AED 36 more than Sami.
How much money did they share altogether? (AED)
questions.ms: Answer: AED 132. M1 for the difference being 7 − 4 = 3 parts. M1 for 36 ÷ 3 = 12 (one part). A1 for 11 × 12 = 132.

questions.q:
a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 6 : 5
Write a : b : c in its simplest form.
questions.ms: Answer: 9 : 12 : 10. M1 for making b the same in both ratios: b = 12 (3 : 4 = 9 : 12 and 6 : 5 = 12 : 10). M1 for 9 : 12 : 10 or an equivalent like 18 : 24 : 20. A1 for 9 : 12 : 10.

questions.q:
A jar contains red sweets and green sweets in the ratio 5 : 2. Maya adds 18 green sweets to the jar. Now the ratio of red sweets to green sweets is 5 : 4.
How many red sweets are in the jar?
questions.ms: Answer: 45. M1 for red = 5k, green = 2k (the red sweets don't change). M1 for 5k : (2k + 18) = 5 : 4, so 20k = 10k + 90 (or: red is 5 parts in both ratios, so the green goes from 2 parts to 4 parts, and 2 parts = 18). A1 for k = 9, red = 45. (Check: 45 : 36 = 5 : 4.)

questions.q:
7 metres of fabric cost AED 59.50.
Work out the cost of 12 metres of the same fabric. (AED)
questions.ms: Answer: AED 102. M1 for 59.50 ÷ 7 = 8.50 (cost of one metre). A1 for 12 × 8.50 = 102. Find the cost of 1 first, then multiply.

questions.q:
Orange juice is sold in three ways.
A: one 330 ml can for AED 2.75
B: one 1.5 litre bottle for AED 11.85
C: a pack of 6 cans of 330 ml for AED 14.40
Which is the best value for money? You must show how you decide.
questions.ms: Answer: C, the pack of 6 cans. M1 for a comparable value for at least two options, e.g. cost per 100 ml: A = 0.833, B = 0.79, C = 0.727 (or ml per AED: 120, 126.6, 137.5). Watch the units: 1.5 litres = 1500 ml and 6 × 330 = 1980 ml. M1 for all three correct. A1 for C with all three values shown. No working: 0 marks.

questions.q:
Here is a recipe for 12 cupcakes:
150 g butter
225 g sugar
3 eggs
180 g flour
How much flour is needed to make 30 cupcakes? (g)
questions.ms: Answer: 450 g. M1 for 180 ÷ 12 = 15 g per cupcake (or scale factor 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5). A1 for 450.

questions.q:
Using the same recipe (12 cupcakes: 150 g butter, 225 g sugar, 3 eggs, 180 g flour).
Yahia has 400 g of butter, 500 g of sugar, 10 eggs and plenty of flour.
What is the greatest number of cupcakes he can make?
questions.ms: Answer: 26. M1 for working out how far each ingredient goes, e.g. butter 400 ÷ 150 × 12 = 32, sugar 500 ÷ 225 × 12 = 26.6…, eggs 10 ÷ 3 × 12 = 40. M1 for picking sugar as the ingredient that runs out first. A1 for 26 (you can't make part of a cupcake, so round down, not up to 27).

questions.q:
The exchange rate is £1 = AED 4.62
A pair of trainers costs £85 in London. The same trainers cost AED 410 in Dubai.
In which city are the trainers cheaper, and by how much in AED? Write the city in your working and type the difference in AED in the answer box.
questions.ms: Answer: London, by AED 17.30. M1 for 85 × 4.62 = 392.70 (or 410 ÷ 4.62 = £88.74). M1 for comparing: 410 − 392.70. A1 for London and AED 17.30. (Comparing in pounds: London cheaper by £3.74 gets M1 M1 A0, because it asks for AED.)

questions.q:
Yahia changes AED 1215 into euros. The exchange rate is €1 = AED 4.05
How many euros does he get? (€)
questions.ms: Answer: €300. M1 for 1215 ÷ 4.05 (divide, because each euro costs 4.05 dirhams). A1 for 300. Multiplying (4920.75): 0 marks; check the answer makes sense, euros are worth more than dirhams so you get fewer of them.
